skill.name: activecampaign-automation
skill.description: Manage ActiveCampaign contacts, tags, list subscriptions, automation enrollment, and contact tasks through Rube MCP.
skill.summary: Guides Rube MCP actions for common ActiveCampaign CRM and marketing automation tasks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around MCP tool names, parameters, and code fences in SKILL.md. One low-risk network finding is confirmed because setup directs users to connect to https://rube.app/mcp as a third-party MCP server. I found no prompt injection text or evidence of shell execution in the skill file.

remediation.suggestion: Disclose that Rube MCP is external and ask users to verify trust before sending CRM data.
Add explicit guidance to confirm authorization before changing contacts, tags, lists, automations, or tasks.

remediation.issue: Static scanner noise from Markdown backticks
remediation.suggestion: Keep tool names clear, but avoid unnecessary fenced blocks if marketplace scanners treat Markdown as executable syntax.

content.value_statement: ActiveCampaign work often needs precise tool choices for contacts, tags, lists, automations, and tasks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows with current schemas.
actual_capabilities: Search for contacts by email, ActiveCampaign ID, or phone number.
Create contacts with email, name, phone, organization, job title, and tags.
Add or remove tags by contact ID or contact email.
Subscribe or unsubscribe contacts from ActiveCampaign list IDs.
Enroll existing contacts into active automation workflows.
Create contact tasks with due dates, task types, assignees, notes, and status.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active ActiveCampaign connection.
Cannot create ActiveCampaign automations; it only enrolls existing contacts.
Some list, automation, user, and task type IDs must be resolved outside the skill.
Bulk changes must respect account rate limits and user authorization.

use_cases.title: Maintain CRM Contacts
use_cases.description: Find existing contacts or create new records before sales and marketing workflows run.

use_cases.title: Manage Campaign Membership
use_cases.description: Apply tags and list subscription changes after forms, events, or segmentation reviews.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Follow-Up Work
use_cases.description: Enroll contacts in automations and create dated follow-up tasks for sales teams.

prompt_templates.title: Find or Create a Contact
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ActiveCampaign Automation skill to find the contact at <email>. If no exact match exists, create the contact with these fields: <fields>.

prompt_templates.title: Update Tags and List Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Find <email>, then add the tags <tags>. Subscribe the contact to list ID <list_id> after confirming the contact identity.

prompt_templates.title: Enroll an Existing Contact
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that <email> exists in ActiveCampaign. Enroll the contact in automation ID <automation_id> only after confirming the automation is active.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bulk CRM Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these contacts and planned actions: <contacts_and_actions>. Search current tool schemas first, identify missing IDs, and ask before making bulk changes.

output_examples.input: Add the prospect tag to Jordan Lee and confirm list membership.
output: Found Jordan Lee by email and confirmed the contact ID.
Added the prospect tag to the contact.
Confirmed the requested list ID before changing subscription status.

output_examples.input: Enroll an existing customer in the renewal automation.
output: Verified that the customer contact exists.
Checked that the provided automation ID is active.
Submitted the enrollment request and summarized the result.

output_examples.input: Create a follow-up task for a contact next Tuesday at 2 PM Eastern.
output: Resolved the contact to an ActiveCampaign contact ID.
Converted the due date to an ISO 8601 datetime with timezone.
Created the task with the selected task type and assignee.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP tools first so parameters match current schemas.
Confirm contact identity before changing tags, subscriptions, automations, or tasks.
Use real ISO 8601 datetimes with timezone offsets for contact tasks.
anti_patterns: Running bulk CRM changes without explicit approval.
Guessing list, automation, user, or task type IDs.
Using placeholder dates, list names, or automation names where IDs are required.

faq.question: Does this skill need ActiveCampaign credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs an active ActiveCampaign connection through Rube MCP before workflows can run.

faq.question: Can it create ActiveCampaign automations?
faq.answer: No. It can enroll contacts into existing active automations, but automation creation happens in ActiveCampaign.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support bulk contact changes?
faq.answer: It provides bulk tagging guidance. Users should confirm actions and respect ActiveCampaign rate limits.

faq.question: What data can it change?
faq.answer: It can change contacts, tags, list subscriptions, automation enrollment, and contact tasks.

faq.question: Why should tools be searched first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change. Searching first helps select current parameters and required fields.
